rationale: First OO-review wave (M60 addendum 2026-09-25: the block-pointer-parameter declaration pin — `runBlock`, with the parameter's declared name forbidden as a read and its call pinned, plus the local argument read that proves the name resolves): OC-E bare-identifier value reads (parameters, body locals incl. bare declarators, same-file ivars/properties, file globals incl. pointer declarators; receivers + arguments inside sends), OC-B category extensions never export (swift precedent: the Trim category must not export the extended class name NSString), OC-D C type-inventory parity (struct/enum/typedef). Every pin probe-verified against both the analyzer and the deriveObjcEdges oracle before pinning; lanes confirm the pair agrees on corpora. OC-E BINDING SPELLING (family contract, DARTD8; `BINDING_SEP` + `metadata.localBinding`, src/ast/types.ts:190). A unit-local read names a binding, not a declaration: the store publishes no parameters or locals, so the bare name could never be answered, and where a same-named declaration existed elsewhere in the project the read was bound to THAT declaration (2,002 such false links measured over the whole 262-file admitted population). The pin below is the spelling the analyzer actually emits, read off `binding-spelling-dump.ts`, and is the form dart (`local-read/reads.expectation.json`) and php already pin. Superseded copy of this file as it stood before the change: `bare-value-reads.expectation.superseded-fb93f6f18.json`. The binding spelling is pinned in BOTH directions: the local reads carry the claim, and the three reads whose names THIS FILE publishes (`store`, `_count`, `gItems`) stay bare and are asserted NOT to carry `meta.localBinding` — an over-reaching claim would turn a correct link into an unbound one.

M60 (#D-fix): a block-pointer parameter's DECLARED NAME is never a read. Pre-fix the analyzer published this edge from the declaration line alone (`void (^handler)(NSString *)`, no read in the function) — the mutant objc/emit-param-decl-as-bare-read re-emits exactly that shape. The `calls runBlock -> handler` pin above proves the parameter resolves: this is a declaration-name gate, not a missing binding.

OC-E BINDING BOUNDARY, negative half: a unit-local read must NOT keep the bare spelling. The bare target is what let the store bind this read to an unrelated same-named declaration; reverting the binding spelling would restore that false link and this forbid fires on it.

OC-E BINDING BOUNDARY, over-reach half: `store` is an IVAR this file publishes, so the name denotes a declaration the store can bind and the bare spelling is correct. A binding claim here would be false and would destroy a correct link — the over-reach the analyzer's `publishedNames` test refuses.

OC-E BINDING BOUNDARY, over-reach half: `_count` is an ivar this file publishes, so the name denotes a declaration the store can bind and the bare spelling is correct. A binding claim here would be false and would destroy a correct link — the over-reach the analyzer's `publishedNames` test refuses.

OC-E BINDING BOUNDARY, over-reach half: `gItems` is a file-scope GLOBAL this file publishes, so the name denotes a declaration the store can bind and the bare spelling is correct. A binding claim here would be false and would destroy a correct link — the over-reach the analyzer's `publishedNames` test refuses.
